question: A 26-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 26 weeks’ gestation, comes to the emergency department because of pain and swelling in her right calf. Physical examination shows an increased circumference of the right calf. The leg is warm and tender on palpation. Dorsiflexion of the right foot elicits calf pain. An ultrasound of the right leg shows a noncompressible popliteal vein. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for this patient's condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Increased circumference of right calf" -> "Warm and tender on palpation" -> "Noncompressible popliteal vein on ultrasound" -> "Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) likely" -> "Risk of pulmonary embolism" -> "Anticoagulation therapy indicated" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Pain and swelling in right calf" -> "Dorsiflexion elicits calf pain" -> "Symptoms consistent with DVT" -> "Heparin indicated for acute treatment" -> 90%
enhanced_information: The patient likely has deep vein thrombosis (DVT) based on clinical presentation and ultrasound findings. Anticoagulation therapy is indicated to reduce the risk of pulmonary embolism. Heparin is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for acute treatment of DVT in this scenario.
analysis: The patient's presentation with pain, swelling, warmth, tenderness, and a noncompressible popliteal vein on ultrasound is highly suggestive of deep vein thrombosis (DVT). The standard pharmacotherapy for acute treatment of DVT is anticoagulation therapy. Among the options provided, heparin is the most appropriate choice for this patient's condition.
